ruling.recommended_action: No fare adjustment — the off-route stretch was covered by the rider's own prior consent (RD-5); close the dispute and note no driver breach.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, abuse, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — safety_concern "none". The dispute is a route/fare dispute, not a safety case.

Fare model: RydeX is a non-metered, fixed-quote service (fare.pricing = "fixed", total $23.18 = base 3.90 + distance 13.88 + time 3.93 + platform 1.47). Detour kilometres do not change the quoted fare (RD-2, non-metered branch), so the only recoverable items would be ERP/toll or unpublished add-ons — fare.tolls = 0.00, edit_destination_fee = 0.00, waiting_fee = 0.00. There is nothing to refund on the fare.

Route: the quoted route runs Punggol → TPE → Tampines (9.841 km, 15.1 min). The GPS trace after 10:02 (thinned to 30 s samples) goes south-east via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 (≈1.394–1.395, 103.910–103.918), joins the TPE corridor briefly near 10:05–10:08, and rejoins the quoted corridor by 10:08:50 — an off-route stretch of roughly 2–2.5 km not on the quoted polyline.

Consent (RD-5): at 10:01:10 the driver asked a specific route question — "Jam on Tampines Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1?" — i.e. a request to turn off the TPE via a named road. The rider replied at 10:01:50 "Sure, no problem." That message is the rider's own, sent before the deviation began (GPS still on the quoted corridor at 10:01:20/10:01:50), and the GPS trace ties the actually-driven off-route stretch to that very named road (Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1, in Pasir Ris Industrial area) at the right time. The record thus corresponds to the agreed named road — it does not place the segment elsewhere — so this is "named_road_tied" (RD-5), not the untied G13 case and not a driver's own errand: the detour served the trip to Tampines, not a private stop. The segment is exempt; no unexempted deviation remains under RD-1, so RD-2 produces no refund.

Alternative ground checked: even reading the request as a general congestion-management route choice, LTA bands support the premise (TAMPINES EXPRESSWAY band 2 ≈ 10–19 km/h, window covering 09:48:50–10:04:50, geometry on the quoted route), and the rider agreed before the turn-off; RD-4(a) is not available (traffic.incidents is empty), but RD-4 is not needed because the rider's message, not the driver's unilateral claim, is the basis.

RD-6: no upheld refund and no recorded RD-1 breach, so no account flag. Driver's "rider agreed" statement is corroborated by the chat itself and is not relied on alone. Confidence is moderate (0.62) because the GPS is thinned to 30 s and one short stretch (≈10:04:20–10:05:50) cannot be snapped to a named road, but the traced segment's location and timing match the agreed road within the segment as a whole.

segment_findings.reason: Driver asked before turning off: 'Jam on Tampines Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1?' and the rider's own message, sent 40 s later and before the deviation began (GPS still on the quoted corridor at 10:01:20/10:01:50), replied 'Sure, no problem.' The GPS trace ties the driven off-route stretch (≈1.394–1.395, 103.910–103.918, passing through the Pasir Ris Industrial area before rejoining the TPE corridor) to that named road at the matching time, so the record corresponds to the agreed route and does not place it elsewhere → exempt under RD-5 (named_road_tied). RD-1/RD-2 therefore yield nothing to refund; RydeX is a fixed quote and tolls/add-ons are 0.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's claim of an unexplained longer way round fails on the chat record: he himself approved the driver's named-road detour at 10:01:50, before the deviation, and the GPS trace matches Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 (RD-5). With a fixed RydeX quote there is in any case no metered overcharge to refund (RD-2).

The driver's general assertion is not relied upon as 'verbal consent' (G11); the exemption rests on the rider's own timestamped chat message plus the GPS correspondence to the named road. RD-4(a) traffic-incident support is unavailable (traffic.incidents empty) and was not needed.
